text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y dollars.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provide(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
Applicant(x) ::: x is a GRE applicant.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has economic hardship.
LiveIn(x, y) ::: x lives in a y.
SingleParentFamily(x) ::: x is a single-parent family.
HaveFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
OutOfWork(x) ::: x is out of work.
Apply(x, y) ::: x is applying to take y.
Premises:
Cost(greTest, 205) ∧ Cheaper(greTest, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Applicant(x) ∧ Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x)) → Provide(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((LiveIn(x, SingleParentFamily) ∨ HaveFewResources(x)) → Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x))) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
LiveIn(tom, SingleParentFamily) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
OutOfWork(dadOfTom) ∧ HaveFewResources(tom) ::: Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
Apply(tom, greTest) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Cheaper(greTest, 300) ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
